published.source: Amcrest IP5M-T1179EW-AI-V3 spec sheet (2025-10-30) and Dahua IPC-HDW2541T-S (S2) datasheet
published.sensor: 1/2.7" progressive CMOS (part and pixel pitch not published)
published.readout_assumption: 1080p is the full 2960x1668 active area scaled by 0.6486 (same 16:9 aspect, and the frame shows the full ~111 deg width, so not a crop)
published.note: FOV figures of a wide lens include its barrel distortion, so the pinhole reading of them (f = half-size / tan(half-angle)) is far below f from focal length / pixel pitch; the published H/V/D are also mutually inconsistent (no single mapping fits all three).

estimated.principal_point_note: assumed at the frame centre (not estimated)

distortion.model: division, p_u - c = (p_d - c) / (1 + l1 r^2 + l2 r^4), r = |p_d - c| / 1000 px

estimated.f_from_registration_note: poorly constrained: 3-4 model landmarks with +/-20-35 mm uncertainty per camera, so f trades off against camera distance; not adopted

f_from_chip_tray_homography.method: chip tray as a planar target: grid-to-image homographies from out/chip_tray.json, pocket centres undistorted with the division model above, homography refit, f from the orthogonality constraint with the principal point at the centre (independent of pocket pitch); computed by tray_focal.py

adopted.why: f = 1070 +/- 45 px from the images: the chip-tray homographies (1062 and 1089 px) and lower registration residuals than at 950 px (cam0 6.5 vs 7.6 px, cam1 0.8 vs 1.4 px on points; ducts 20/4.6/5.8 vs 26/8.2/5.5 px). It is 13-18 % above the sensor-based 908-935 px, which fits a 1080p stream scaled from a central ~2560x1440 window rather than the whole 2960x1668 area (not confirmed by any published source); with the measured distortion it gives the published 58 deg vertical FOV exactly
